To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) RefineNet is a generic multi path network that can be used for any semantic segmentation task, (ii) it can be trained end to end and (iii) it outperforms state of the art methods on seven different datasets.

(a) RefineNet is a generic multi path network that can be used for semantic segmentation of high resolution images; (b) it achieves new state of the-art results on multiple datasets, including the most recent Cityscapes dataset; (c) it is the first method that achieves over 80\% intersection over union score on the PASCAL VOC2012 segmentation dataset; and (d) the code for our implementation is made publicly available.

(1) RefineNet is a generic network for semantic segmentation that is able to achieve state of the art performance in all the datasets we evaluated on; (2) RefineNet exploits all available information to enable high resolution predictions using long range residual paths; (3) The individual components of the network employ residual connections following an identity mapping mindset, and; (4) Chained residual pooling is an efficient mechanism to capture rich background context.
